# Supported formats

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_format_docs.py from plugin metadata. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every plugin's options can be set with `-O key=value`, in `[plugins.options.<name>]` of
`artifactdiff.toml`, in the web UI, or via the API's `options` field. Severities are documented
heuristics to help triage — not verdicts. See also [limitations.md](limitations.md).

| Plugin | Extensions | Extra |
|---|---|---|
| [JSON](#json) | `.json`, `.geojson`, `.jsonld`, `.webmanifest`, `.ipynb` | `core` |
| [CSV / TSV](#csv) | `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.tab`, `.psv` | `tabular` |
| [Apache Parquet](#parquet) | `.parquet`, `.pq` | `tabular` |
| [SQLite](#sqlite) | `.sqlite`, `.sqlite3`, `.db`, `.db3` | `core` |
| [Raster images](#image) | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.tif`, `.tiff`, `.bmp`, `.gif` | `image` |
| [Audio](#audio) | `.wav`, `.flac`, `.ogg`, `.oga`, `.mp3`, `.aiff`, `.aif`, `.opus` | `audio` |
| [PDF](#pdf) | `.pdf` | `pdf` |
| [glTF / GLB 3D models](#gltf) | `.glb`, `.gltf` | `gltf` |
| [safetensors (ML weights)](#safetensors) | `.safetensors` | `safetensors` |
| [Text (line diff)](#text) | `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.rst`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.toml`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `.conf`, `.xml`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.css`, `.svg`, `.properties`, `.env`, `.log`, `.tex`, `.graphql`, `.gql`, `.proto`, `.sql`, `.py`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.sh`, `.tf`, `.hcl`, `.jsonl`, `.ndjson` | `core` |
| [Binary (fallback)](#binary) | any | `core` |

## json

**JSON** — Structural comparison of JSON documents (configs, API schemas, model configs).

Compares parsed documents, so formatting and key order never count as changes.
Paths are JSONPath-like (`$.model.layers[2].weights`, `$["odd key"]`); `details.pointer` holds the
RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. Arrays: **lcs** aligns elements by content (an insertion is one change, not a
cascade), **index** compares by position, **key** matches objects by a field and reports reorderings
as `moved`. Integer vs. float literals with equal value (`1` vs `1.0`) are an `info` change; booleans
are never equal to numbers. Duplicate keys produce a warning.

Severity: type change **high** · removed key/element **medium** · added **low** · value change **low**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `array_strategy` | `lcs` \| `index` \| `key` | `"lcs"` | lcs: align elements by content (detects insertions); index: compare by position; key: match objects by `array_key`. |
| `array_key` | string \| null | `null` | Object field identifying array elements (strategy 'key'). |
| `ignore_paths` | list[string] | `—` | Glob patterns such as '$.meta.*'. |
| `float_tolerance` | number | `0.0` | Absolute tolerance for numeric comparisons. |
| `max_size_mb` | number | `256` | JSON is parsed in memory; larger files are rejected. |

Limitations:
- JSON documents are parsed fully in memory (bounded by max_size_mb).

Capabilities: `structural-diff`, `json-pointer`, `array-lcs`, `array-key-matching`, `ignore-paths`.

## csv

**CSV / TSV** — Row- and column-level dataset comparison with optional primary keys.

Cell values are compared as the exact text in the file; column types are *inferred* (Polars) and type
changes are reported separately. With a primary key (explicit, or auto-selected `id`/`uuid`/`key`/`pk`
when unique and non-null in both files — always with a warning), rows are joined and modified rows list
the changed cells. Without a key, rows are compared as a multiset of full-row hashes: a changed row is
one removal plus one addition, never a guessed pairing. Duplicate keys or null keys fall back to the
multiset with a warning. Also reported: added/removed/reordered columns, delimiter, duplicate-row count,
missing values per column, and mean/std/min/max/distinct changes beyond `stats_threshold` (descriptive
statistics, not significance tests).

Severity: removed column / type change **medium** · added column, row changes **low** · statistics **info**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `primary_key` | list[string] \| null | `null` | Column(s) identifying a row. Without one, rows are matched by full content. |
| `auto_key` | boolean | `true` | If no primary_key is set, use a column named id/uuid/key/pk when it is unique and non-null in both files (a warning says so). |
| `delimiter` | string \| null | `null` | Default: sniffed. |
| `has_header` | boolean | `true` | First line contains column names. |
| `encoding` | `utf8` \| `utf8-lossy` | `"utf8"` | utf8-lossy replaces invalid bytes instead of failing. |
| `null_values` | list[string] | `—` | Extra strings treated as missing. |
| `ignore_columns` | list[string] | `—` | Columns excluded from all comparisons. |
| `max_row_changes` | integer | `500` | Rows listed individually (all are counted). |
| `compare_statistics` | boolean | `true` | Compare per-column descriptive statistics. |
| `stats_threshold` | number | `0.05` | Relative change that makes a statistic reportable. |
| `infer_rows` | integer | `10000` | Rows used for type inference. |

Limitations:
- Column types are inferred from a sample of rows; they are not declared by the CSV format.
- Without a primary key, a modified row is reported as one removal plus one addition.

Capabilities: `schema-diff`, `row-diff`, `primary-key`, `statistics`, `duplicates`, `streaming`.

## parquet

**Apache Parquet** — Schema, nullability, metadata, record and statistics comparison for Parquet files.

Schema and metadata come from the Parquet footer (no data read): column additions/removals, Arrow type
changes, nullability, column order, row count, compression, row groups, writer. Records are compared like
CSV (primary key or row multiset) over columns whose type did not change; statistics over numeric columns.
Polars' streaming engine processes row groups in chunks.

Severity: removed column / type change **high** · nullability **medium** · added column, row changes **low**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `primary_key` | list[string] \| null | `null` | Column(s) identifying a record. |
| `auto_key` | boolean | `true` | Use a unique, non-null id/uuid/key/pk column if present. |
| `ignore_columns` | list[string] | `—` | Columns excluded from all comparisons. |
| `compare_records` | boolean | `true` | Disable to compare schema and statistics only. |
| `max_row_changes` | integer | `500` | Rows listed individually (all are counted). |
| `compare_statistics` | boolean | `true` | Compare per-column descriptive statistics. |
| `stats_threshold` | number | `0.05` | Relative change that makes a statistic reportable. |

Limitations:
- Columns whose type changed are excluded from record matching (values are not comparable).
- Nested (list/struct) columns are compared by whole-value hash, not element by element.

Capabilities: `schema-diff`, `nullability`, `row-diff`, `primary-key`, `statistics`, `chunked`.

## sqlite

**SQLite** — Schema and data comparison of SQLite databases (opened read-only).

Opened strictly read-only. Schema: tables, columns (declared type, NOT NULL, default, primary-key
position), constraint/option changes in `CREATE TABLE`, indexes, triggers and views (whitespace-normalised
SQL). Data: tables with an identical declared primary key are compared by a streaming merge-join ordered
by that key (memory does not grow with table size); other tables as row multisets, or by `rowid` if
`match_by_rowid` is enabled (with a warning — rowids change after `VACUUM`). Values must match in storage
class too (`1` vs `'1'` is a change). Also compares `user_version`, `application_id`, encoding, page size.

Severity: removed table/column **high** · type/constraint/index/trigger changes **medium** · additions, rows **low**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compare_data` | boolean | `true` | Compare table contents (not only the schema). |
| `tables` | list[string] | `—` | Only compare these tables (default: all). |
| `ignore_tables` | list[string] | `—` | Tables excluded from data comparison. |
| `match_by_rowid` | boolean | `false` | For tables without a primary key, match rows by rowid (unstable after VACUUM). |
| `max_row_changes` | integer | `200` | Rows listed per table (all are counted). |

Limitations:
- Views and virtual tables are compared by definition only; their contents are not queried.
- Tables without a primary key are compared as row multisets (a changed row = removal + addition) unless match_by_rowid is enabled.

Capabilities: `schema-diff`, `index-diff`, `trigger-diff`, `view-diff`, `row-diff`, `streaming`, `read-only`.

## image

**Raster images** — Pixel, structural (SSIM), perceptual-hash and metadata comparison of raster images.

Visual differences (category `visual`) are reported separately from metadata (`metadata`). With equal
dimensions, pixels are compared in strips: a pixel changed if any RGBA channel differs by more than
`tolerance`. Changed pixels are grouped into `region_block`-sized blocks; 8-connected blocks form regions
with bounding boxes. Metrics: changed pixels and ratio, max and mean channel difference, **SSIM**
(Wang et al. 2004, grayscale, 7×7 uniform window, on images downscaled to `ssim_max_side`) and **dHash
distance** (Hamming distance of 64-bit difference hashes; size-independent). These are measurements, not
probabilities. Assets: previews, heatmap (black → red → yellow → white), overlay with region boxes.
Metadata: format, mode, ICC profile (hash), DPI, EXIF tags, PNG text chunks, frame count.

Severity of the pixel change: < 1 % of pixels **low**, < 10 % **medium**, otherwise **high**; dimensions **high**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tolerance` | integer | `0` | Per-channel difference ignored (8 suits JPEG noise). |
| `ignore_alpha` | boolean | `false` | Compare RGB only. |
| `ignore_metadata` | boolean | `false` | Skip EXIF, DPI and text-chunk comparison. |
| `region_block` | integer | `8` | Block size (px) used to group changed pixels. |
| `max_regions` | integer | `50` | Changed regions listed individually (largest first). |
| `max_pixels` | integer | `100000000` | Images with more pixels are rejected. |
| `ssim` | boolean | `true` | Compute SSIM (costs time on large images). |
| `ssim_max_side` | integer | `1024` | Images are downscaled to this size before SSIM. |
| `preview_max_side` | integer | `512` | Size of generated previews and heatmaps. |

Limitations:
- Pixels are compared after conversion to 8-bit RGB(A); higher bit depths are quantised.
- Only the first frame of multi-frame images (GIF, multi-page TIFF) is compared.
- Pixel-level comparison requires identical dimensions; otherwise only metadata and the perceptual hash are compared.

Capabilities: `pixel-diff`, `ssim`, `perceptual-hash`, `regions`, `heatmap`, `overlay`, `metadata`.

## audio

**Audio** — Duration, format, level, silence, spectral and waveform comparison of audio files.

Decoded block by block with libsndfile. Reports format/subtype, sample rate, channels, duration, RMS and
peak level (dBFS — not LUFS), leading/trailing/total silence (segments below `silence_threshold_db`),
energy per octave band from averaged Hann-windowed FFT power spectra of the mono mix (bands below
`spectral_floor_db` in both files are skipped), and — with equal sample rate and channel count — the
sample-wise difference: max absolute difference, difference RMS, signal-to-difference ratio, first
differing sample and the time ranges where the difference exceeds `difference_threshold_db`. Assets:
waveform envelopes and log-frequency spectrograms. No semantic interpretation of the audio is attempted.

Severity: sample rate/channels **high** · duration **medium** · level, silence, waveform ranges **low** · spectral bands **info**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `segment_seconds` | number | `0.1` | Analysis segment length. |
| `silence_threshold_db` | number | `-60` | Segments below this RMS (dBFS) are silent. |
| `min_silence_seconds` | number | `0.3` | Shortest silent stretch listed as an interval. |
| `level_tolerance_db` | number | `0.5` | RMS/peak changes below this are ignored. |
| `spectral_tolerance_db` | number | `1.5` | Per-band energy changes below this are ignored. |
| `spectral_floor_db` | number | `-80` | Bands below this level in both files are not compared. |
| `difference_threshold_db` | number | `-60` | Difference RMS (dBFS) marking a segment changed. |
| `max_segments` | integer | `20` | Differing time ranges listed individually. |
| `max_duration_seconds` | number | `14400` | Longer recordings are rejected. |
| `max_fft_windows` | integer | `4000` | FFT windows analysed per file (sub-sampled beyond). |

Limitations:
- Levels are RMS/peak dBFS, not perceptual loudness (LUFS).
- Sample-level waveform comparison needs equal sample rates and channel counts.
- No semantic understanding of audio content (speech, music, instruments) is attempted.
- MP3/Opus support depends on the libsndfile build (see `artifactdiff doctor`).

Capabilities: `duration`, `loudness`, `silence`, `spectrum`, `waveform-diff`, `spectrogram`, `streaming`.

## pdf

**PDF** — Page, text, layout, embedded-image, metadata and rendered visual comparison of PDF documents.

Pages are aligned by their extracted text (LCS), so an inserted page is one addition. Matched pages are
compared line by line, by media-box size, by image objects (count and placement), and visually: both
pages are rendered by PDFium at `render_dpi` and compared pixel by pixel (changes above
`min_changed_ratio`), with previews and an overlay for the first `max_preview_pages`. Document
information (Title, Author, …; `ModDate` ignored by default) and PDF version are compared. Pages with
images but no text layer trigger a "looks scanned" warning: no OCR is performed.

Severity: removed page / page size **medium** · added page, text, images, render **low** · metadata **info**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visual_compare` | `all` \| `changed` \| `none` | `"all"` | Render matched pages and compare pixels: all pages, only text-changed pages, or none. |
| `render_dpi` | integer | `50` | Resolution used for visual page comparison. |
| `pixel_tolerance` | integer | `16` | Per-channel difference ignored when rendering. |
| `min_changed_ratio` | number | `0.0005` | Rendered pages below this are equal. |
| `max_rendered_pages` | integer | `50` | Matched pages rendered for visual comparison. |
| `max_preview_pages` | integer | `6` | Pages with visual previews in the report. |
| `max_pages` | integer | `5000` | Documents with more pages are rejected. |
| `ignore_metadata` | list[string] | `—` | Metadata keys not compared (ModDate changes on every save). |
| `max_text_changes_per_page` | integer | `20` | Text changes listed per page (all are counted). |

Limitations:
- Only the PDF text layer is compared; scanned pages need OCR, which ArtifactDiff does not perform.
- Embedded images are compared by count and placement, not by pixel content (rendering covers visuals).
- Password-protected PDFs are not supported.

Capabilities: `page-alignment`, `text-diff`, `page-size`, `image-objects`, `metadata`, `render-diff`.

## gltf

**glTF / GLB 3D models** — Scene-graph, transform, mesh-geometry, material, texture and bounds comparison of glTF 2.0.

glTF 2.0 (`.gltf` JSON or `.glb`) is parsed directly. Nodes, meshes, materials and images are matched by
name (unnamed ones by index, with a warning). Reported: added/removed objects and meshes, renames (only
when exactly one removed/added pair has identical geometry hash and transform; confidence 0.9), local
transform changes, mesh reassignment, hierarchy changes, vertex/face counts, vertex attributes, material
assignment, geometry changes (SHA-256 of positions + indices — equal counts never imply equal meshes; with
equal counts the max vertex displacement and number of moved vertices are reported), material factors and
texture references, embedded texture content (hash/size/MIME/pixel size), counts of animations, skins,
cameras and lights, extensions, and the world-space scene bounding box. A wireframe preview (front/top) is
generated for reports; the web UI shows both models in a synchronized 3D viewer.

Severity: removed object/mesh, geometry and count changes **medium** · additions, transforms, materials **low**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `transform_tolerance` | number | `1e-06` | Absolute tolerance for transform components. |
| `geometry_tolerance` | number | `0.0` | Max vertex displacement treated as unchanged. |
| `material_tolerance` | number | `1e-06` | Absolute tolerance for numeric material factors. |
| `detect_renames` | boolean | `true` | Report unique geometry+transform matches as renames. |
| `max_json_mb` | number | `64` | Larger glTF JSON is rejected. |
| `preview` | boolean | `true` | Render a wireframe preview (front/top) for reports. |
| `max_preview_triangles` | integer | `50000` | Triangles drawn per model in the wireframe preview. |

Limitations:
- Only glTF 2.0 is supported; Draco/meshopt-compressed and sparse accessors are not decoded.
- External .bin/texture files are compared only when they sit next to the model file.
- Animations, skins and cameras are compared by count only.

Capabilities: `scene-graph`, `transforms`, `geometry-hash`, `vertex-displacement`, `materials`, `textures`, `bounding-box`, `rename-detection`, `wireframe-preview`.

## safetensors

**safetensors (ML weights)** — Tensor-level comparison of .safetensors model weights with chunked numerical statistics.

Validated with the official `safetensors` library, header bounds-checked, then tensors are read in
`chunk_elements` chunks (memory independent of tensor size; BF16 supported). Reports metadata changes,
added/removed tensors (with dtype, shape, parameters and statistics), renames (removed/added pair with
equal dtype/shape and byte-identical data, unique; confidence 0.95), dtype and shape changes, total
parameter count and file size. For changed tensors: min/max/mean/std of both versions, L2 difference,
max absolute difference, relative difference ‖new−old‖/‖old‖ and the number of differing elements
(beyond `atol`). Byte-identical tensors are counted, not listed. Weights are never executed.

Severity: dtype/shape **high** · removed tensor, parameter count **medium** · value changes by relative
difference: < 1e-3 **low**, < 0.1 **medium**, otherwise **high**.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compare_values` | boolean | `true` | Read tensor data (disable for header-only comparison). |
| `compute_stats` | boolean | `true` | Report min/max/mean/std for changed, added and removed tensors. |
| `atol` | number | `0.0` | Absolute tolerance per element. |
| `chunk_elements` | integer | `1048576` | Elements read per chunk. |
| `detect_renames` | boolean | `true` | Report unique byte-identical removed/added tensors as renames. |

Limitations:
- FP8 tensors are compared byte-wise; numerical statistics are not computed for them.
- Rename detection requires byte-identical data; renamed *and* modified tensors appear as removed + added.

Capabilities: `tensor-diff`, `dtype`, `shape`, `statistics`, `l2-difference`, `rename-detection`, `chunked`.

## text

**Text (line diff)** — Line-based comparison for text formats without a dedicated plugin.

Fallback for text formats without a dedicated plugin (YAML, TOML, Markdown, XML, source code, and
unknown files that look like text). Line diff via `difflib`; reports encoding and line-ending changes.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignore_whitespace` | boolean | `false` | Ignore leading/trailing whitespace on each line. |
| `ignore_case` | boolean | `false` | Compare lines case-insensitively. |
| `max_size_mb` | number | `64` | Text files above this size are rejected. |
| `max_lines_exact` | integer | `50000` | Above this many lines difflib's faster 'autojunk' heuristic is used. |

Limitations:
- Text is compared line by line without understanding its syntax.

Capabilities: `line-diff`.

## binary

**Binary (fallback)** — Byte-level comparison used when no format-specific plugin applies.

Fallback for everything else: size change and the exact differing byte ranges (found with a streaming
XOR scan), plus appended/truncated tails. The meaning of the bytes is unknown, which the result says.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_regions` | integer | `20` | Differing byte ranges listed individually. |
| `merge_gap` | integer | `16` | Ranges closer than this many bytes are merged. |
| `chunk_size_kb` | integer | `1024` | Streaming chunk size. |

Limitations:
- No format-specific plugin was used: only raw bytes were compared, so the meaning of changes is unknown and an insertion shifts every following byte.

Capabilities: `byte-ranges`, `streaming`.
